### 2026-10-14 – ## Began CADing for Starting Clamp Project

**4.5h**

## Began CADing for Starting Clamp Project

journaling for 4.5 hours total, across two days

I got some solid work done on my tennis starting my clamp project.

Since I was inspired and impressed by [this](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4597862) 3d printed flying clamp I found on thingiverse, my design is following its core mechanism for firmly clamping a tennis string against a force that could be up to 60 lbs.

Basically all starting clamps you can buy have the same basic design, spring loaded plier handles connected to textured, high friction plates that squeeze the string to hold it in place while tension is pulled. However I'm doing something quite different because It would be practically impossible to 3d print springs that can provide enough clamping force. Also, I think that the overall design is just generally flawed and would be especially bad if it were made with plastic.

My plan is to use a tensioning lever and adjustable knob through two plates that uses the natural flex of plastic to clamp a string with an adjustable level of force. This is how the flying clamps in the link above work. It could be slightly less convinent to have to latch and unlatch the lever whenever you want to clamp, but it should still have all the same capabilites of any other starting clamp and also be less harsh on softer tennis strings.

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 171156](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9xdf2FmmiIyTpo5aVb7w67R43kQ7Kd0m/35edf161cc072e927596dfcc12b035d458d0756326dcb2e0fd333c44bec7c9f2.png)

I began designing one of the plates that will clamp the string. so far I'm assuming that both plates will be identical but I'm not completely sure yet.

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 093101](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9xdf2FmmiIyTpo5aVb7w67R43kQ7Kd0m/5b43e92943c11f024094671ef50dec06c7830aed086a3e48a8836536044f6e5c.png)

it has an area that is inset slightly by 0.2 mm where I will glue a piece of sand paper to provide the nessesary friction on the string where it will clamp.

I have a through hole near the bottom of the handle where I will have the lever and knob mechanism to clamp the plates together. It is closer to the bottom to make better use of the flex of the plastic plates.

there is another inset area near the top that is inset where I will put a simple 3d printed square spring to force the plates apart when the lever isn't latched down.

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 093020](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9xdf2FmmiIyTpo5aVb7w67R43kQ7Kd0m/8a67c5e8d174ee4e8cfe5f2d13ea1beee21f65c69515bacfc0efa6073a2991ed.png)

My familiarity with cadding isn't great so I know the sketch was done atrociously, but up to this point, at least everything was fairly straightforward.

The problems began when I decided to attack the screw knob portion

my plan was to create the knob first with the threads on the inside using the helix tool and a sweep, and then use that part with a boolean remove operation to create the corresponding threads on the dowel that connects through the plates. unfortunately I kept getting errors that said the boolean failed to generate valid geometry.

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 100316](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9xdf2FmmiIyTpo5aVb7w67R43kQ7Kd0m/299703936702c57f2e762d17f317d1e0de536ec1ed9b48ca75b0330e620b6371.png)
![Screenshot 2026-10-14 102525](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9xdf2FmmiIyTpo5aVb7w67R43kQ7Kd0m/fd2dbb595c43e55d566aa5735db82268d8872fd920944746075410bcac574f5e.png)

I tried tweaking dimensions to see if that would fix some weird edges that might be causing the failure, but I couldn't figure it out so I ended up making the threads for the dowel first and creating the knob with corresponding internal threads seprately. But this ended up being not the worst because it was easy to create a bit of spacing tolerance on the internal threads of the knob, instead of them just being ideal boolean opposites of each other.

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 153235](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9xdf2FmmiIyTpo5aVb7w67R43kQ7Kd0m/74e68a7b23762fe3fb507227aceec21b01cb1d14addfacf9f57f7c20ec45f6ea.png)

up next I'm going to finalize the exact dimensions of the knob, and design the lever and spring

TLDR; I'm cading a 3d printing a starting clamp for stringing tennis rackets. the design is slightly atypical and based on a flying clamp. so far I've designed the clamping and screwing portions.
